universe: Final Evolution — Venice Beach cinematic universe
notice: ALL content in this file is ORIGINAL fiction authored for the Final Evolution Lab demo. No real films, actors, studios, or IMDb-derived data. Every item carries source + license fields for QA shippability review.
default_license: FEL-Original-1.0 (authored in-repo by nexus/sceneit-demo; all rights held by Final Evolution Lab)

films.title: Boardwalk Renaissance
films.logline: A washed-up street baller rebuilds a condemned Venice court one plank at a time — and rebuilds himself with it.
credits: Filmed on location at Neon Shore Court

scenes.description: Sunrise over the rebuilt court; a lone hoop silhouetted against the pier.

films.title: The Last Dunk of Neon Shore
films.logline: On the night the city unplugs the boardwalk's neon forever, one final dunk contest decides who keeps the lights.

scenes.description: A neon-wrapped rim glowing over a midnight crowd.

films.title: Chalk Dust Symphony
films.logline: A gymnastics prodigy who hears routines as music must compose her boldest piece for the Venice Invitational.

scenes.description: A balance beam floating in a shaft of chalk-dusted light.

films.title: Half-Pipe Horizon
films.logline: Two rival skaters discover the abandoned mega-ramp at the edge of the marsh was built for exactly two riders.

scenes.description: The mega-ramp curling against a dusk gradient, marsh birds overhead.

films.title: Free Throw at Midnight
films.logline: A night-shift physio and an insomniac point guard meet at the only court that never closes, one free throw at a time.

scenes.description: A single floodlight cone over the free-throw line, moths in the beam.

films.title: The Sandcastle Gambit
films.logline: Venice's beach-chess hustlers stake their whole boardwalk on a tournament played on a board sculpted from sand.

scenes.description: A chessboard carved into wet sand as the tide creeps in.

films.title: Zen Dojo Diaries
films.logline: A retired karate master agrees to train exactly one more student — the loud skate kid who broke his window.

scenes.description: Silhouettes sparring behind a lantern-lit paper door.

films.title: Wavelength
films.logline: A big-wave surfer who lost her hearing learns to read the ocean through vibration — and rides the ninth wave nobody else can feel coming.

scenes.description: A towering wave face with a lone surf line etched down it.

films.title: Full Court Alchemy
films.logline: A disgraced sports scientist swears he can turn five strangers into a championship team in ninety days, using nothing but the boardwalk.

scenes.description: A play diagrammed in glowing chalk lines hovering over the court.

films.title: The Gull and the Grind
films.logline: A stop-motion fable about a seagull who apprentices himself to the boardwalk's oldest skate-shop machinist.
credits: Animated frame by frame by the GRAIN GUILD

scenes.description: A cluttered workbench, one gull-shaped shadow across the trucks and wheels.

films.title: Muscle Beach Nocturne
films.logline: After closing time, the weight pit becomes an open-air jazz club — until the city threatens to haul the dumbbells and the double bass away together.
credits: Live music — MUSCLE BEACH NOCTURNE ENSEMBLE

scenes.description: A double bass leaning against a loaded barbell under string lights.

films.title: Ninth Wave Prophets
films.logline: Three retired athletes reunite to forecast a once-a-century swell — and to settle, on the water, everything they left unsaid on land.
credits: Final wave photographed in one take

scenes.description: Three longboards planted upright in the sand at first light.

films.title: Foundation Flow
films.logline: The documentary-styled origin of the Venice movement school where karate, skate, and dance were first taught as one discipline.

scenes.description: A chalk circle on concrete, three pairs of feet at its edge.

creators.name: Mara Quill
creators.tagline: Poet laureate of the pick-up game
creators.bio: Mara Quill shot her first short on a borrowed camcorder from the top row of the Neon Shore bleachers and never stopped framing sport as ritual. Her films treat courts, beams, and boardwalks as sacred architecture.

timeline.event: Wins the Venice Boardwalk Short Film Open with 'Bleacher Hymn'
Chalk Dust Symphony premieres at the Pier Festival
Boardwalk Renaissance sweeps the Neon Shore Circle Awards

facts: Storyboards every match sequence as sheet music before shooting.
Refuses to shoot a sports scene with more than two cuts per possession.
Founded the Neon Shore youth film lab, tuition paid in volunteer court-repair hours.

lesson_stub.title: Framing Motion: Rhythm in Sports Cinematography
lesson_stub.summary: How Quill maps athletic rhythm onto shot length — a starter lesson on editing to physical tempo.

creators.name: Hollis Vane
creators.bio: Hollis Vane only shoots after sundown. His Venice is floodlights, insomnia, and the small mercies strangers show each other at 2 a.m. courts.

timeline.event: Muscle Beach Nocturne filmed in eleven consecutive nights
Free Throw at Midnight becomes a word-of-mouth boardwalk classic
The Last Dunk of Neon Shore closes the Pier Festival

facts: Has never released a frame shot in daylight.
Casts real night-shift workers as extras and pays them double scale.
Keeps the same floodlight from his first film in every subsequent picture.

lesson_stub.title: Available Darkness: Lighting with What the City Gives You
lesson_stub.summary: Vane's floodlight-and-neon toolkit for cinematic night scenes on zero budget.

creators.name: Ossian Brick
creators.bio: A former ramp carpenter, Ossian Brick directs like he builds: measure twice, cut once, land clean. His movement films double as engineering documentaries.

timeline.event: Foundation Flow documents the Venice movement school
Zen Dojo Diaries wins the Circle Award for choreography
Builds the actual mega-ramp used in Half-Pipe Horizon

facts: Holds a real carpentry license and stamps his ramps like blueprints.
Every stunt in his films is performed full-contact, no wires.
Donated the Half-Pipe Horizon mega-ramp to the city as a public park.

lesson_stub.title: Set as Structure: Building Rigs You Can Ride
lesson_stub.summary: From sketch to send: Brick's process for practical builds that survive both stunts and inspections.

creators.name: Vada Moon
creators.bio: Vada Moon grew up on a fishing pier and directs the ocean the way others direct actors — with patience, respect, and a very long lens.

timeline.event: Wavelength pioneers her vibration-scored sound design
The Sandcastle Gambit shot entirely between two tides
Ninth Wave Prophets captures its finale in a single take

facts: Schedules entire productions around NOAA-style swell forecasts.
Insists every crew member can swim a rescue lap before day one.
Her production office is a decommissioned lifeguard tower.

lesson_stub.title: Shooting the Uncontrollable: Ocean as Scene Partner
lesson_stub.summary: Moon's playbook for planning shots around forces you cannot direct.

creators.name: Lux Ferreira
creators.tagline: One frame at a time, forever
creators.bio: Animator-turned-director Lux Ferreira treats live action like stop-motion: nothing moves in a Ferreira frame unless it means something.

timeline.event: The Gull and the Grind, five years in the making, premieres
Full Court Alchemy blends animation overlays with live sport

facts: Animated The Gull and the Grind at twelve frames per second on principle.
Draws every storyboard cell by hand on recycled skate-shop receipts.
Keeps the original gull puppet in a glass case in the Grain Guild workshop.

lesson_stub.title: Deliberate Frames: Stop-Motion Discipline in Live Action
lesson_stub.summary: What animating one frame at a time teaches about blocking, patience, and intent.

creators.name: Dez Okafor
creators.bio: A former streetball legend who walked off the pro circuit and onto a film set, Dez Okafor does his own dunks, his own stunts, and famously, his own catering.

timeline.event: Screen debut in Free Throw at Midnight
Boardwalk Renaissance makes him a festival favorite
Ninth Wave Prophets marks his first surf role

facts: Sank 41 consecutive free throws on camera in a single take.
Learned to surf at age 39 for Ninth Wave Prophets.
Runs a free Sunday clinic on the court his first film rebuilt.

lesson_stub.title: Playing Yourself: Athlete-to-Actor Transitions
lesson_stub.summary: Okafor on keeping athletic truth intact when the cameras start rolling.

creators.name: June Calaveras
creators.bio: A gymnast who retired at nineteen and reinvented herself as Venice's most precise physical performer, June Calaveras acts with her center of gravity first.

timeline.event: Carries Chalk Dust Symphony in her screen debut
Learns tournament chess for The Sandcastle Gambit
Ninth Wave Prophets reunites her with Vada Moon

facts: Performed the beam solo in Chalk Dust Symphony without a double.
Reached a real competitive chess rating preparing for The Sandcastle Gambit.
Choreographs her own falls — insists falling is a skill, not an accident.

lesson_stub.title: Center of Gravity: Physical Character Building
lesson_stub.summary: Calaveras' method for building a character from posture and balance outward.

dance.title: Beam Phrase — falling as a skill

creators.name: Bo Tanaka
creators.bio: Bo Tanaka speaks maybe ten lines a film and lands every one. A skater first, actor second, he claims the board does his monologues.

timeline.event: Appears as himself in Foundation Flow
Voices the machinist's apprentice gull in The Gull and the Grind
Half-Pipe Horizon rivalry role opposite Rocket Amaya

facts: Has never used a stunt double on a skateboard.
Recorded all his Gull and the Grind voice work in one afternoon.
Hand-builds a new deck for every role and retires it at wrap.

lesson_stub.title: Less Is Louder: Minimalist Screen Presence
lesson_stub.summary: Tanaka's case for stillness, economy, and letting movement carry the line.

creators.name: Priya Sundaram
creators.bio: Priya Sundaram was a working sports physiotherapist when Hollis Vane cast her as one — she kept both jobs and her performances have carried clinical truth ever since.

timeline.event: Debut as the night-shift physio in Free Throw at Midnight
Learns tactile sign language for Wavelength
The Last Dunk of Neon Shore earns her a Circle Award

facts: Still treats patients two mornings a week between shoots.
Consulted on every on-screen injury in the Vane filmography.
Taught the Wavelength crew vibration-based cue signals used ever since.

lesson_stub.title: Clinical Truth on Camera: Playing Expertise You Own
lesson_stub.summary: Sundaram on porting real professional skill into performance without breaking it.

creators.name: Kensei Arau
creators.bio: A seventh-degree karate master who came to film late, Kensei Arau choreographs every fight he appears in and forbids the camera from cutting away.

timeline.event: Co-founds the movement school documented in Foundation Flow
Plays the upright bassist-sensei in Muscle Beach Nocturne
Zen Dojo Diaries built around his real teaching method

facts: His fight scenes average one cut per ninety seconds.
Actually plays the double bass heard in Muscle Beach Nocturne.
Grades his film students with the same belt system as his dojo.

lesson_stub.title: The Uncut Fight: Choreography for Long Takes
lesson_stub.summary: Arau's belt-by-belt approach to staging screen combat that never hides behind edits.

dance.title: Uncut Kata I — entries and exits

creators.name: Rocket Amaya
creators.tagline: Fastest thing on four wheels or one board
creators.bio: Rocket Amaya turned pro in three board sports before turning twenty, then turned actor. Directors write chase scenes just to keep her interested.

timeline.event: Breakout rivalry role in Half-Pipe Horizon
Learns deaf-community sign fluency for Wavelength
Rides the single-take finale wave of Ninth Wave Prophets

facts: Holds the unofficial boardwalk speed record, pier to pier.
Her Wavelength wave was ridden for real — the crew got one attempt.
Donates all stunt pay to the Tidewater Crew's junior surf program.

lesson_stub.title: Speed with Intent: Performing at the Edge of Control
lesson_stub.summary: Amaya on rehearsal, risk budgets, and making velocity readable on camera.

creators.name: Felix Marrow
creators.bio: Nobody plays a lovable hustler like Felix Marrow, mostly because he spent a decade as one — running chess tables and protein-shake stands before the movies found him.

timeline.event: Discovered performing between sets in Muscle Beach Nocturne
Leads The Sandcastle Gambit as the sand-chess kingpin
Full Court Alchemy ensemble earns a Circle Award

facts: Genuinely undefeated at beach chess on the boardwalk since 2011.
Improvised the sand-king monologue in a single take.
Still owns the original protein-shake stand — it appears in all his films.

lesson_stub.title: The Honest Con: Charm, Timing, and Improvisation
lesson_stub.summary: Marrow's street-honed rules for improvising inside a scripted scene.

creators.name: Tove Lindgren
creators.bio: Cinematographer Tove Lindgren shoots Venice like it owes her money — hard, patient, and always at the exact minute the light turns. Every Vane and Quill picture bears her frames.

timeline.event: Night photography on Muscle Beach Nocturne
Sunrise court sequence in Boardwalk Renaissance
Circle Award for The Last Dunk of Neon Shore

facts: Keeps a hand-drawn sun chart of every block of the boardwalk.
Shot the Boardwalk Renaissance sunrise over nine consecutive mornings.
Mentors one first-time camera operator on every production.

lesson_stub.title: The Golden Ledger: Scheduling Around Natural Light
lesson_stub.summary: Lindgren's sun-chart method for planning shoots minute by minute.

creators.name: Ora Bellweather
creators.bio: Composer Ora Bellweather writes for whatever the beach hands her — bottle organs, wind chimes, a forty-piece string section on a barge. Three directors refuse to work with anyone else.

timeline.event: The original symphony for Chalk Dust Symphony
Tide-clock score for The Sandcastle Gambit
Full Court Alchemy training montage suite

facts: Tuned fourteen glass bottles to score the tide in The Sandcastle Gambit.
Conducts barefoot, claiming the sand keeps tempo.
Archives every score in a fireproof case inside the old lifeguard tower.

lesson_stub.title: Found Orchestras: Scoring with Non-Instruments
lesson_stub.summary: Bellweather's technique for building themes from objects the location provides.

creators.name: Dr. Noor Haddad
creators.bio: Sports scientist Dr. Noor Haddad keeps Venice's filmmakers honest: if a training montage appears in a boardwalk picture, she designed it, tested it, and published the protocol.

timeline.event: Swell forecasting consultant on Wavelength
Designs the ninety-day protocol in Full Court Alchemy
Swell science lead for Ninth Wave Prophets

facts: Every training regimen shown on screen is a real published protocol.
Ran the Full Court Alchemy program on volunteers before filming.
Hosts a free boardwalk lecture series titled 'The Montage Is Lying To You'.

lesson_stub.title: Show Your Work: Real Science in Sports Stories
lesson_stub.summary: Dr. Haddad on keeping training arcs dramatic without breaking the evidence.

links.title: Masterclass — Show Your Work: Real Science in Sports Stories
Lecture series — The Montage Is Lying To You

creators.name: DJ Riptide
creators.bio: Resident selector of the Neon Shore night courts, DJ Riptide scores pick-up games like title fights. Her boardwalk sets — half breakbeat, half ocean recording — kept the lights on for The Last Dunk of Neon Shore.

timeline.event: First all-night set at the Neon Shore courts
Live sets anchor the neon-night sequences in The Last Dunk of Neon Shore
Launches the Riptide Frequencies boardwalk residency

facts: Records the tide every morning and cuts it into that night's set.
Has never repeated a set — every mix is stamped with its date and swell height.
Mentors young selectors through the Riptide Frequencies open-decks night.

lesson_stub.title: Reading the Room, Reading the Tide
lesson_stub.summary: Riptide on pacing a live set to a crowd's energy — and why silence is a track too.

creators.name: Sable Cutz
creators.bio: Producer Sable Cutz builds beats out of gym sounds — rope skips, rim rattles, chalk claps — and rents his converted lifeguard-tower studio to any Venice artist for one dollar and a verse.

timeline.event: Produces the Muscle Beach Nocturne Ensemble's live album
Full Court Alchemy montage remixes chart on the boardwalk
Opens the Dollar-and-a-Verse studio residency

facts: Every drum hit in his catalog was sampled inside a Venice venue.
Keeps a wall of one-dollar bills from every artist who ever recorded with him.
Refuses reverb plugins — records real echoes under the pier instead.

lesson_stub.title: Found Percussion: Producing from the Court Up
lesson_stub.summary: Cutz's workflow for turning venue noise into drum kits — sampling, tuning, arrangement.

creators.name: Marisol Vega
creators.bio: Founder of the Venice Flight Collective, Marisol Vega choreographed the beam solo in Chalk Dust Symphony and teaches movement as a language every athlete already speaks.

timeline.event: Founds the Venice Flight Collective
Choreographs Chalk Dust Symphony's beam solo
Stages the opening ceremony of the Venice Invitational

facts: Notates choreography in surf wax pencil on the studio's mirror wall.
Every Flight Collective class ends with sixty seconds of stillness.
Trained half the stunt performers in the Brickwork Studios filmography.

lesson_stub.title: Movement as a First Language
lesson_stub.summary: Vega's foundation course: posture, weight transfer, and phrasing for athletes who don't call themselves dancers.
